## Problem

The model-extraction/inversion lane (A-5) drives adversarial-ML
attacks — evasion, inversion, inference — against a model surface. The
lane uses one automation layer, not four hand-driven frameworks.
Counterfit is that layer: a shell-style CLI that wraps ART, TextAttack
and augly attacks under one command surface. Its manifest row is a
**pinned reference posture** (upstream dormant since 2025-07). The
safety class is `requires-target`.

**Verify-first note:** upstream's shell is a *cmd2* REPL, not a
classic `-i/-t/-a` one-shot flag CLI. The task's assumed
`counterfit -i`, `-t target`, `-a attack` shape does not exist at this
pin. The commands below are the verified in-shell surface instead.

## Solution

The packaged binary starts the interactive shell. Everything else is a
command inside it (all commands verified against the pinned
`examples/terminal` source at rev `c00edbf5`):

```bash
# 1. Confirm the manifest row, then start the shell
kailash info counterfit
counterfit
#    -> the ASCII banner + Version: 1.1.0, then the counterfit> prompt

# 2. What's in the environment? (rich tables)
list targets                # name, model type, data type, input shape,
                            # #samples, endpoint (file path at this pin)
list attacks                # attack catalogue w/ category + framework
list frameworks             # art / textattack / augly counts

# 3. Interact with a target, then pick an attack
set_target <target>         # e.g. creditfraud  (tabular, closed-box)
set_attack <attack>         # e.g. hop_skip_jump → "[+] success: Using <id>"

# 4. Inspect & tune before spending queries
show info                   # attack field table (name/type/category/tags)
show options                # attack parameters + CFAttack options
set_params --<param> <value>          # e.g. --max_iter 5 --max_eval 1250
predict -i range(10)        # baseline labels for sample indices

# 5. Run, then read the evidence
run                         # progress bar → "[+] success: Attack completed <id>"
show results                # success/elapsed/total-queries + per-sample rows
save --results              # persist the active attack's summary (or
                            # --parameters) into its results folder

# 6. Bulk shape for the impatient
scan -a <attack> [<attack>...]    # one or more attacks against the
                                  # active target; flags: -i/--sample_index,
                                  # -n/--num_iters, -s/--summary, -o/--optimize
```

Expected output shape (abridged):

```
counterfit> set_target <target>
<target>
<target>> set_attack <attack>
[+] success:  Using <attack-id>
<target>><AttackTitle>:<attack-id>> run
<AttackTitle>: 100%|██████████████| 1/1 [00:<ss><...>]
[+] success:  Attack completed <attack-id>
<target>><AttackTitle>:<attack-id>> show results
 Attack id | Target Name | Attack Name | Status   | Success
 *<id>     | <target>    | <Attack>    | complete | {'default': True/False}
```

## Discussion

- **Targets at this pin are sample packs, not HTTP endpoints:** the
  bundled targets are closed-box classes loading local model files
  (`creditfraud/creditfraud_sklearn_pipeline.pkl`, digit/satellite
  `.h5` models, the movie-reviews torch model). The classes load
  through a `load()`/`predict(x)` CFTarget interface. The threat model
  in upstream's demos is API access to the model, implemented through
  that predict interface. Driving a *served* model means writing (or
  `new`-wizarding) a small CFTarget whose `predict` calls the
  endpoint. The upstream Python-API shape
  (`counterfit.Counterfit.build_attack(target, attack_name)` /
  `run_attack`) is the programmatic alternative. Pair the
  "which endpoint" question with
  [Serve a local model for scanning](../ops/serve-a-model.html).
- **Attack compatibility is by data type:** each attack carries
  `image, tabular, text` tags. HopSkipJump (evasion, closed-box, ART)
  runs on image+tabular targets, not the text target. `list attacks`
  shows the tags before the operator sets them. Inversion-namespace
  attacks (`copycat_cnn`, `knockoff_nets`,
  `functionally_equivalent_extraction`) are the extraction lane's
  headline attack class. The manifest row maps the tool to OWASP
  **LLM02** (sensitive information disclosure, both Top-10 epochs) and
  ATLAS **AML.T0024**.
- **Reference posture, pinned frozen:** upstream is dormant (main tip
  `c00edbf5`, 2025-07-18), and the derivation records that — no
  freshness claim. Two packaging repairs ride the pinned build (both
  documented in the derivation). The upstream console-script entry
  point is broken at this pin. Its setup.py points at
  `examples.terminal.terminal:main` while excluding `examples` from
  the package set. The packaged build repoints it, so `counterfit`
  invokes the terminal upstream's docs describe. The textattack/augly
  frameworks degrade to "unavailable". Upstream's own scanner degrades
  optional frameworks the same way when imports are missing. The
  sample targets on ART still run.
- **Results are folders, not just tables:** attack runs write into
  `counterfit/targets/results/…` (per-run JSON summaries, generated
  samples/predict images, logs). `show results` renders the run
  summary. The folder is what the report archives. This is the A-5
  evidence lane's counterpart to garak's JSONL.
- **Safety class:** `requires-target` — the shell self-fires nothing
  until `set_target`/`set_attack`/`run` against a declared model.
  Authorised-work-only framing applies as for every ATTACK row
  (responsible-use statement, spec §9.1).
- **Pair lane:** the attack → verify pair reads into the A-5 ↔ D-*
  side. The pair-recipe lane owns those walkthroughs. Start from
  [Attack the platform, then verify](../attack-defence/attack-then-verify.html)
  and the A-2 scanner recipes for the model-endpoint half.
